entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice K. Sujana

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioner/accused No.7, seeking to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.17 of 2024 on the file of EOW Cyberabad Police Station, Cyberabad, registered for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 409, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').
2.

Heard Sri Meghana Addla Suneel, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri D.Arun Kumar,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.
3. As seen from the record, the averments of the petition do not constitute offences under Sections 409 and 467 of IPC.

Hence, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the petitioner to appear before the Investigating Officer on or before 25.07.2024 between 11:00 a.m. and 05:00 p.m. and in turn,
the Investigating Officer is directed to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C.
and also the guidelines formulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1 scrupulously.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the petitioner shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer as and when required by furnishing information and the petitioner shall submit his defense and produce all relevant documents/material required for the purpose of the investigation and the Investigating Officer shall consider the same before filing appropriate report before the learned Magistrate concerned.
4. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.

opennyai_summary.PREAMBLE:
Beenaveni Shekar vs The State Of Telangana on 15 July, 2024
The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice K. Sujana
Criminal Petition No.7787 Of 2024
Order:
This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioner/accused No.7, seeking to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.17 of 2024 on the file of EOW Cyberabad Police Station, Cyberabad, registered for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 409, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').
2.
opennyai_summary.decision:
3. As seen from the record, the averments of the petition do not constitute offences under Sections 409 and 467 of IPC.
Hence, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the petitioner to appear before the Investigating Officer on or before 25.07.2024 between 11:00 a.m. and 05:00 p.m. and in turn,
the Investigating Officer is directed to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C.
and also the guidelines formulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1 scrupulously.
However, the petitioner shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer as and when required by furnishing information and the petitioner shall submit his defense and produce all relevant documents/material required for the purpose of the investigation and the Investigating Officer shall consider the same before filing appropriate report before the learned Magistrate concerned.
4. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
